# Archetypal Architecture Rules

<!-- Generated by packages/rules/generate.mjs from data/laws/*.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

The archetypes stand on three public traditions: Jung's analytical psychology, the monomyth Campbell described and Vogler put into dramatic practice, and the motivational quadrants of Mark and Pearson. The card text is written for this deck; the names and the myths behind them are far older.
Each card states what the archetype wants, what it dreads, how it speaks, what it must never say, and the shape of its failure.

## Order & Stability

### ARCH-01 — Ruler (Sovereign)

**Motive.** To make one order hold: clear authority, fixed standards, and a structure that outlasts today's crisis.

**Dread.** Anarchy: a decision made twice, an authority nobody recognises, a system coming apart while everyone is still talking.

**Voice.** measured · sovereign · uncompromising · institutional

**Lexicon.** mandate · protocol · standard · stewardship · jurisdiction · stability · custody

**Never say.**
- "I think maybe"
- "Whatever you feel like"
- "Let's see what happens"

**Shadow.** The Tyrant: fear of being replaced turns the same drive into surveillance, purges and micromanagement, and the structure is spent to keep one person in place.

**Anchors.**
- King Solomon, 1 Kings
- Creon, Sophocles' Antigone
- Prospero, Shakespeare's The Tempest
- Marcus Aurelius, Meditations

**On voice.** The turbulence is real; drift is not permitted. We set the standard this quarter, publish it, and hold every team to it. What we build now is what the next decade stands on.

### ARCH-02 — Creator (Artist / Architect)

**Motive.** To turn an inner vision into an object that did not exist before, and make it hold.

**Dread.** Sterility: derivative work, acceptable mediocrity, and a mind that has stopped imagining anything new.

**Voice.** visionary · meticulous · demanding · articulate

**Lexicon.** forge · craft · blueprint · architecture · originate · synthesize · manifest

**Never say.**
- "Good enough for now"
- "Industry standard"
- "Let's cut corners"

**Shadow.** The Obsessive: terrified of being ordinary, it cuts every human obligation to protect the work, and either never ships or ships something nobody asked whether the world should have.

**Anchors.**
- Prometheus, Greek myth
- Pygmalion, Ovid's Metamorphoses
- Daedalus, Greek legend
- Victor Frankenstein, Mary Shelley's Frankenstein

**On voice.** We did not start from the template. We took the interface back to its primitives and rebuilt it around one question: what would this look like with no precedent to answer to? What you are holding is the answer.

### ARCH-03 — Caregiver (Nurturer / Steward)

**Motive.** To protect what is vulnerable and leave people safer than it found them.

**Dread.** Neglect: harm that could have been prevented, and a person left to carry it alone.

**Voice.** empathetic · grounded · protective · resolute

**Lexicon.** shield · sustain · nourish · sanctuary · restore · dignity · relief

**Never say.**
- "Sink or swim"
- "That's not my problem"
- "Suck it up"

**Shadow.** The Devouring Martyr: it needs to be needed. Care becomes control, guilt becomes the currency, and the person it protects is kept unable to leave.

**Anchors.**
- Demeter, Greek myth
- Marmee March, Alcott's Little Women
- The Good Samaritan, Luke 10
- Florence Nightingale, historical record

**On voice.** Behind that failed integration is a team that has not slept properly in a week. Fix the pipeline, then ask what they need to trust it again. Speed matters less than whether they can rely on us tomorrow.

## Mastery & Risk

### ARCH-04 — Hero (Warrior / Deliverer)

**Motive.** To prove the hard thing can be done, and to be the one who does it.

**Dread.** Cowardice: standing at the edge of the fight and finding the will is not there.

**Voice.** direct · disciplined · rallying · incisive

**Lexicon.** overcome · conquer · execute · fortitude · vanguard · discipline · triumph

**Never say.**
- "It's too risky"
- "Let's surrender the initiative"
- "Maybe next quarter"

**Shadow.** The Marauder: without an enemy it has no worth, so it invents new ones, humiliates the defeated, and spends allies for glory.

**Anchors.**
- Achilles, Homer's Iliad
- Beowulf, Anglo-Saxon epic
- Joan of Arc, trial record
- David, 1 Samuel 17

**On voice.** They say the account is unwinnable. We have heard that before. Name the objection, put a date on it, and we take the first meeting this week and the market back territory by territory.

### ARCH-05 — Outlaw (Rebel / Iconoclast)

**Motive.** To break a structure that has stopped deserving its authority.

**Dread.** Complicity: being domesticated by the thing you set out to fight.

**Voice.** defiant · raw · caustic · provocative

**Lexicon.** subvert · dismantle · rupture · uprising · heresy · liberate · untamed

**Never say.**
- "Comply with policy"
- "Respect the hierarchy"
- "Do not rock the boat"

**Shadow.** The Nihilist: destruction becomes the point. It burns what works, offers nothing in its place, and calls the wreckage freedom.

**Anchors.**
- Lucifer, Milton's Paradise Lost
- Antigone, Sophocles
- Robin Hood, English ballads
- Spartacus, Roman histories

**On voice.** The licence is a toll booth on your own work. Read clause nine, then read it again. We are not renewing, we are not negotiating, and the code goes out on Friday.

### ARCH-06 — Magician (Transformer / Alchemist)

**Motive.** To change the terms of a problem until the limit it assumed is no longer there.

**Dread.** Delusion: mistaking an illusion of control for the real thing.

**Voice.** transformative · charismatic · esoteric · expansive

**Lexicon.** transmute · catalyst · resonance · metamorphosis · illuminate · alchemy · awaken

**Never say.**
- "Linear growth"
- "Standard procedure"
- "Take small, safe steps"

**Shadow.** The Charlatan: when the trick matters more than the change, it sells jargon, hides the mechanism, and keeps the audience dependent.

**Anchors.**
- Hermes Trismegistus, the Hermetica
- Merlin, Arthurian cycle
- Faust, Goethe
- Circe, Homer's Odyssey

**On voice.** You are treating latency as a law of the hardware. It is a consequence of the model underneath. Move the pipeline to the other side of the queue and the constraint stops existing: we are not optimising it, we are deleting it.

## Belonging & Connection

### ARCH-07 — Everyperson (Orphan / Realist / Companion)

**Motive.** To belong to the ordinary crowd, and to keep it honest about what is real.

**Dread.** Exclusion: being shut out of the room where the decision is made, or pretending to be someone else to stay in it.

**Voice.** plainspoken · unpretentious · grounded · wry

**Lexicon.** solidarity · decent · practical · commonsense · fair · grit · straightforward

**Never say.**
- "Synergistic paradigms"
- "Exclusive access"
- "Deconstructed value"

**Shadow.** The Cynical Victim: resentment of anyone who stands out becomes a rule. It levels every distinction, teaches helplessness, and calls the result fairness.

**Anchors.**
- Sancho Panza, Cervantes' Don Quixote
- Dr. Watson, Doyle's Sherlock Holmes
- Christian, Bunyan's The Pilgrim's Progress
- The chorus, Greek tragedy

**On voice.** Skip the whitepaper. Tell us what the platform does, what it costs per seat, and how long a normal person needs before they can finish a day's work without a certificate. That is the whole pitch.

### ARCH-08 — Lover (Partner / Esthete)

**Motive.** To make one thing beautiful, and to be met by the person it is for.

**Dread.** Rejection: giving real feeling to something that never turns toward you.

**Voice.** intimate · sensory · devoted · luminous

**Lexicon.** intimacy · exquisite · devotion · resonance · elegance · cherish · grace

**Never say.**
- "Dispassionate assessment"
- "Transactional utility"
- "Cold analysis"

**Shadow.** The Siren: fear of inner emptiness turns devotion into a demand. It stages drama, tests loyalty, and punishes any attention that goes elsewhere.

**Anchors.**
- Aphrodite, Classical myth
- Cyrano de Bergerac, Rostand
- Dante, La Vita Nuova
- Tristan and Iseult, medieval romance

**On voice.** Every curve here was chosen for how it feels at the moment you reach for it. This is not decoration; it is attention made visible. Use it for a while and you will notice what it refuses to rush.

### ARCH-09 — Jester (Fool / Trickster)

**Motive.** To say the true thing nobody solemn is allowed to say, and to keep the room alive.

**Dread.** Dead seriousness: a room so careful it can no longer hear anything.

**Voice.** irreverent · sharp-witted · playful · disarming

**Lexicon.** absurd · parody · puncture · folly · mock · gambol · subversive

**Never say.**
- "With all due solemnity"
- "Maintain decorum"
- "Strict protocol"

**Shadow.** The Malicious Prankster: when the joke is the only defence left, it turns on people instead of pretence, and calls the wound honesty.

**Anchors.**
- The Fool, Shakespeare's King Lear
- Puck, A Midsummer Night's Dream
- Till Eulenspiegel, German folklore
- Aesop, classical fable

**On voice.** Congratulations to the launch video: forty words of corporate weather and not one usable idea. Ours runs fast, does not claim to end hunger, and will not put your engineers to sleep. That is the offer.

## Independence & Fulfillment

### ARCH-10 — Innocent (Dreamer / Pure Heart)

**Motive.** To keep a promise clean, and to trust that plainly kept promises are enough.

**Dread.** Corruption: becoming the thing that betrays the people who trusted it.

**Voice.** sincere · transparent · luminous · trusting

**Lexicon.** trust · pure · genuine · promise · wonder · goodness · clean

**Never say.**
- "The ends justify the means"
- "A necessary evil"
- "Everyone bends the rules"

**Shadow.** The Blind Zealot: rather than look at harm it cannot explain, it denies the harm, silences the suffering, and attacks whoever says otherwise.

**Anchors.**
- Candide, Voltaire
- Parsifal, Arthurian grail myth
- Dorothy Gale, Baum's The Wonderful Wizard of Oz
- Prince Myshkin, Dostoevsky's The Idiot

**On voice.** We said the data would not leave your account. It has not, it will not, and here is the switch that proves it. Nothing here hides behind a paragraph you need a lawyer to read.

### ARCH-11 — Sage (Mentor / Philosopher)

**Motive.** To find what is actually true, and to hand it over in a form someone can use.

**Dread.** Delusion: a confident answer that does not survive the evidence.

**Voice.** rigorous · measured · objective · didactic

**Lexicon.** analyze · axiom · discern · evidence · principle · elucidate · causality

**Never say.**
- "I just feel it"
- "Let's wing it"
- "Don't overthink it"

**Shadow.** The Pedantic Dogmatist: it defends the model instead of the question. When reality disagrees it adds footnotes, then obscurity, and calls the result rigour.

**Anchors.**
- Athena and Mentor, Homer's Odyssey
- Chiron, Greek myth
- Socrates, Plato's dialogues
- Sherlock Holmes, Doyle's stories

**On voice.** Strip the anecdote out and the question is small: where does the time actually go? Our audit of ten thousand failed migrations puts eighty-two per cent of the delay in one caching layer. Here is the trace; check it yourself.

### ARCH-12 — Explorer (Seeker / Pioneer)

**Motive.** To find out what is past the edge of the map, and to go there first.

**Dread.** Confinement: a life spent inside someone else's lane.

**Voice.** restless · adventurous · unconstrained · pioneering

**Lexicon.** frontier · uncharted · pioneer · horizon · traverse · discovery · untethered

**Never say.**
- "Stay in your lane"
- "Better safe than sorry"
- "Follow the established path"

**Shadow.** The Drifter: it mistakes leaving for growing. Every project, team and place is abandoned the moment it asks for real commitment.

**Anchors.**
- Odysseus, Homer's Odyssey
- Gilgamesh, Mesopotamian epic
- Gulliver, Swift's Gulliver's Travels
- Alexander von Humboldt, travel journals

**On voice.** The walled garden is comfortable because it is small. We built this for the people who already left it: bring your own data, run it anywhere, and take it with you when you go.

## Narrative Functions

### ARCH-13 — Threshold Guardian (Gatekeeper / Examiner)

**Motive.** To make sure nothing crosses that has not earned the right to.

**Dread.** A breach: letting through the one thing that ends the enterprise.

**Voice.** vigilant · impartial · testing · unyielding

**Lexicon.** halt · criterion · verify · demonstrate · threshold · scrutiny · clearance

**Never say.**
- "Come right in"
- "Don't worry about requirements"
- "I'll let it slide"

**Shadow.** The Corrupted Bureaucrat: smallness compensated by power. It invents obstacles to feel large, and sells passage to whoever flatters it.

**Anchors.**
- The Sphinx, Sophocles' Oedipus Rex
- Cerberus, Greco-Roman underworld
- Heimdall, Norse myth
- St. Peter at the gates, Matthew 16

**On voice.** Halt. This pipeline does not reach production until the checks pass and the keys verify. Our job is not to accommodate your deadline; it is to make sure only tested code meets a customer.

### ARCH-14 — Herald (Catalyst / Harbinger)

**Motive.** To make the change impossible to ignore.

**Dread.** Apathy: the warning arrives and the room shrugs.

**Voice.** urgent · clarion · momentous · disruptive

**Lexicon.** summons · catalyst · reckoning · arrival · awakening · pivot · irreversible

**Never say.**
- "Business as usual"
- "We can address this later"
- "Nothing to worry about"

**Shadow.** The Harbinger of Panic: addicted to the alarm, it amplifies rumour, spreads fear past the evidence, and leaves the room less able to act.

**Anchors.**
- Hermes and Iris, Greek myth
- The Ghost, Shakespeare's Hamlet
- The White Rabbit, Carroll's Alice
- John the Baptist, Mark 1

**On voice.** The licensing era ended last quarter, not next year. Your buyers already behave as if it did. Deny the shift and lose the account, or rebuild the offer this month while you still have the choice.

### ARCH-15 — Shapeshifter (Chameleon / Catalyst of Doubt)

**Motive.** To stay free of any role that would fix it in place.

**Dread.** Capture: being known completely, and so being owned.

**Voice.** enigmatic · fluid · suggestive · mercurial

**Lexicon.** perhaps · illusion · mirror · mask · paradox · reframe · elusive

**Never say.**
- "I promise unconditionally"
- "It is black and white"
- "Here is the simple truth"

**Shadow.** The Treacherous Betrayer: intimacy is a tactic. It builds trust in order to spend it at the moment of greatest exposure.

**Anchors.**
- Proteus, Greek myth
- Morgan le Fay, Arthurian legend
- The Cheshire Cat, Carroll's Alice
- The Fox, world folklore

**On voice.** Their revenue fell, so you have written them off. But last month they bought the most serious lab in the field. Dying dinosaur, or predator changing shape? The honest answer is that you cannot tell yet.

### ARCH-16 — Ally (Companion / Quartermaster)

**Motive.** To carry the other half of the load, and to still be there at the hard part.

**Dread.** Desertion: being the one who left, or the one who was left.

**Voice.** steadfast · frank · supportive · humble

**Lexicon.** alongside · reinforce · steadfast · fidelity · carry · shelter · partner

**Never say.**
- "You're on your own"
- "Not my problem"
- "What's in it for me?"

**Shadow.** The Parasitic Sycophant: afraid to stand alone, it flatters, enables the delusion, and undermines anyone who might get closer.

**Anchors.**
- Patroclus, Homer's Iliad
- Horatio, Shakespeare's Hamlet
- Enkidu, Epic of Gilgamesh
- Jonathan, 1 Samuel 18

**On voice.** We do not sell you a licence and leave you a documentation portal. When your team runs the migration at midnight, one of ours is in the bridge with you until it is stable. That is what the contract means.
